n2-set-11-q-1.translation: While living a night-owl lifestyle, I ended up developing a sleep disorder.
n2-set-11-q-1.correctAnswerEnglish: shougai / 睡眠障害 - sleep disorder / impairment

choices.reason: shoukai is 紹介 (introduction); 害 is read gai, not kai.
jougai is 場外 (outside the grounds); 障 is read shou, not jou.
shougai is the correct on'yomi reading of 障害 (disorder, impairment, disability).
joukai misreads both characters.

n2-set-11-q-2.translation: The amount of solar energy that falls upon the Earth in one hour is equivalent to the amount consumed by humankind in an entire year.
n2-set-11-q-2.correctAnswerEnglish: soutou / 相当 - equivalent to / corresponding to

choices.reason: soutou is the correct on'yomi reading of 相当, meaning equivalent or corresponding to.
shoutou misreads 相 as shou; here it is read sou.
aitou means condolence (哀悼).
souou is 相応 (appropriate or suitable).

n2-set-11-q-3.translation: As the birthrate declines, there is a strong tendency for parents to anticipate and preemptively assist their children.

choices.reason: keikou is the correct on'yomi reading of 傾向 (tendency, trend, inclination).
katakou uses kun'yomi kata- for 傾, which does not form this on'yomi compound.
keimuki uses kun'yomi muki for 向, which is incorrect in this compound.
katamuki is the standalone kun'yomi noun 傾き (tilt, slant, slope).

n2-set-11-q-4.translation: I believe that if I continue to polish and refine my strengths, I will surely succeed.
n2-set-11-q-4.correctAnswerEnglish: migaki / 磨き - polishing / refining / honing

choices.reason: tataki means striking or beating (叩き).
kagayaki means shining or brilliance (輝き).
iki is not a reading of 磨.
migaki is the correct kun'yomi reading of 磨き (stem of 磨く, to polish or hone).

n2-set-11-q-5.translation: Humans are better able to demonstrate their potential when confronted with difficulties.
n2-set-11-q-5.correctAnswerEnglish: hakki / 発揮 - demonstration / exhibition (of strength, talent, ability)

choices.reason: hakkou means publication or issue (発行).
hakki is the correct on'yomi reading of 発揮 (demonstrating or displaying abilities).
hokko is an incorrect reading.
hokki means launching or originating a project (発起).

n2-set-11-q-6.translation: Nearly 30 countries around the world have suffered damage from an international robbery ring.
n2-set-11-q-6.correctAnswerEnglish: goutou / 強盗 - robbery / robber / burglary

choices.reason: 監獄 means prison or jail.
強罰 is not a recognized Japanese word.
強盗 is the correct kanji for goutou (robbery, armed robbery, or robber).
獄盗 is not a valid Japanese compound.

n2-set-11-q-7.translation: A car was developed that automatically engages the brakes and halts immediately before a collision.
n2-set-11-q-7.correctAnswerEnglish: shoutotsu / 衝突 - collision / crash / impact

choices.reason: 衝突 is the correct kanji compound for shoutotsu (collision, crash, or impact).
障 means obstacle or barrier, not collision.
衡 means balance or scale.
将 means commander, general, or future.

n2-set-11-q-8.translation: She is the type of person who devotes herself completely to the one she loves.
n2-set-11-q-8.correctAnswerEnglish: tsukusu / 尽くす - to devote oneself / do one's utmost for

choices.reason: 注 is read sosogu or chuu, meaning to pour or focus.
就 is read tsuku or shuu, meaning to take up a post.
尽くす is the correct kanji for tsukusu (to devote, serve, or do one's utmost).
着 is read kiru, tsuku, or chaku, meaning to wear or arrive.

n2-set-11-q-9.translation: Paying respect to the partner country's culture is crucial in international cooperation.
n2-set-11-q-9.correctAnswerEnglish: keii / 敬意 - respect / esteem; 敬意を払う = to pay respect

choices.reason: 仰 means to revere or look up, but does not form 仰意.
掲 means to post, publish, or hoist.
傾 means to tilt, lean, or incline.
敬意 is the correct kanji compound for keii (respect or honor).

n2-set-11-q-10.translation: The system should be revised so that people can conduct job hunting as new graduates for several years after graduation.
n2-set-11-q-10.correctAnswerEnglish: aratameru / 改める - to reform / revise / amend

choices.reason: 改める is the correct kanji for aratameru (to reform, revise, or change a system for the better).
政 is read sei, shou, or matsurigoto (politics/governance).
敢 is read aete or kan (daring/bold).
変める is not a valid word; the verb is 変える (kaeru).

n2-set-11-q-11.translation: That rookie athlete has the highest level of attention.
n2-set-11-q-11.correctAnswerEnglish: do / 注目度 - degree of attention / profile

choices.reason: 注目感 is not a standard Japanese compound.
注目性 is not used; 話題性 (topicality) exists, but 注目 pairs with 度.
注目料 would imply a monetary fee for paying attention.
注目度 (chuumokudo) means the level, degree, or intensity of attention received.

n2-set-11-q-12.translation: Mobile phones have become astonishingly high-performance over the past ten years.
n2-set-11-q-12.correctAnswerEnglish: kou / 高性能 - high performance / sophisticated capability

choices.reason: 高性能 (kouseinou) is the established prefix compound for high performance or high capability.
最性能 does not exist (最高性能 exists, but 最 cannot attach directly to 性能 alone).
名性能 is not a valid compound.
長性能 does not exist; 長寿命 (long life) exists, but 性能 pairs with 高.

n2-set-11-q-13.translation: This is still nothing more than a draft proposal.
n2-set-11-q-13.correctAnswerEnglish: an / 計画案 - draft plan / tentative proposal

choices.reason: 計画済 means already planned or settled, which contradicts に過ぎません (nothing more than).
計画下 is not standard; under planning is 計画中.
計画案 (keikakuan) means a draft proposal or tentative plan.
計画的 is an adjective meaning planned or deliberate, which does not take the copula phrase に過ぎません this way.

n2-set-11-q-14.translation: Tomorrow I will separate from the group and act independently.
n2-set-11-q-14.correctAnswerEnglish: betsu / 別行動 - separate action / acting independently

choices.reason: 代行動 is not a Japanese expression.
異行動 is not used.
単行動 is not used; 単独行動 exists, but 単 alone does not attach to 行動.
別行動をとる (betsukoudou o toru) is the standard collocation for taking separate action away from a group.

n2-set-11-q-15.translation: If there hadn't been a fire extinguisher in the kitchen, it would probably have turned into a full fire.

choices.reason: 消火機 is not used for portable fire extinguishers (器 is used for handheld appliances/containers).
消火器 (shoukaki) is the standard term for a fire extinguisher.
消火技 means fire-extinguishing technique or skill.
消火基 is not a word.

n2-set-11-q-16.translation: If you turn left at the traffic light about 50 meters ahead, the sea will come into view.
n2-set-11-q-16.correctAnswerEnglish: zenpou / 前方 - ahead / forward direction

choices.reason: 正面 means direct front or facade, but is not used with distance vectors like 50メートル前方.
後者 means the latter.
前方 (zenpou) means ahead or forward, naturally combining with distance indicators (約50メートル前方).
先頭 means the head or front of a queue/column.

n2-set-11-q-17.translation: At this party, the formal attire for men is a tuxedo.

choices.reason: 正式な服装 means formal attire or dress code.
正確 means precise or accurate.
正道 means the proper/righteous path.
正規 means regular, authorized, or formal status (e.g. 正規社員, regular employee).

n2-set-11-q-18.translation: That professor answers questions sarcastically, so he is disliked.
n2-set-11-q-18.correctAnswerEnglish: hiniku / 皮肉 - sarcastic / cynical / ironic

choices.reason: 適切 means appropriate or suitable, which would be well-received, not disliked.
残念 means regrettable or unfortunate.
器用 means dexterous or skillful.
皮肉な答え方 means a sarcastic or cynical way of responding, which explains why he is disliked.

n2-set-11-q-19.translation: (In a letter) As the weather has turned cold, please take very good care of yourself.
n2-set-11-q-19.correctAnswerEnglish: kereguremo / くれぐれも - sincerely / earnestly / by all means

choices.reason: たびたび means frequently or repeatedly.
どうにか means somehow or other.
かなり means considerably or quite.
くれぐれも is the formal epistolary adverb used to earnestly request or caution someone regarding health.

n2-set-11-q-20.translation: The economy is slow to recover, and citizens are disappointed with the cabinet.

choices.reason: 失業 means unemployment.
失望している means being disappointed or losing hope in someone or an institution.
失脚 means downfall or being ousted from office (a cabinet falls, citizens do not 失脚 the cabinet).
失礼 means discourteous or rude.

n2-set-11-q-21.translation: My mother was fortunate to have crossed paths with a trustworthy doctor.
n2-set-11-q-21.correctAnswerEnglish: meguri / 巡り会えて - happened to meet / encountered by fortune

choices.reason: 立ち会う means to be present at or witness an event.
兼ね会う is not a valid Japanese compound.
巡り会う (meguriau) means to encounter or meet someone fortuitously through fate.
触れ合う means to come into physical contact or emotionally connect with someone.

n2-set-11-q-22.translation: It seems this problem is not as simple as I thought, and resolving it may take time.
n2-set-11-q-22.correctAnswerEnglish: shinpuru / シンプル - simple / straightforward

choices.reason: ハード means hard or difficult; saying it is 'not hard' would contradict taking time to solve.
ワイド means wide or broad.
ユニーク means unique.
シンプル (simple) fits the context of not being as straightforward as expected, thereby taking more time.

n2-set-11-q-23.translation: Ms. Tanaka has become even more beautiful lately.
n2-set-11-q-23.correctAnswerEnglish: masumasu / ますます - increasingly / even more

choices.reason: 急に means suddenly.
少しだけ means just a little.
ますます means increasingly or even more, which paraphrases 一段と (ichidanto, a notch more / markedly more).
まあまあ means passably or so-so.

n2-set-11-q-24.translation: His sales performance has been sluggish lately.
n2-set-11-q-24.correctAnswerEnglish: fuchou da / 不調だ - in a slump / underperforming

choices.reason: 上がった means improved or went up.
落ちた means dropped in a single event, while ふるわない describes an ongoing sluggish condition.
順調だ means proceeding smoothly or favorably.
不調だ means in poor condition, performing poorly, or in a slump, matching ふるわない.

n2-set-11-q-25.translation: He is an individual who cannot be judged by ordinary yardsticks.
n2-set-11-q-25.correctAnswerEnglish: kijun / 基準 - criterion / standard / yardstick

choices.reason: 表現 means expression or phrasing.
基準 means standard or criterion, matching the figurative usage of ものさし (ruler / benchmark).
常識 means common sense.
方法 means method or means.

n2-set-11-q-26.translation: Using other people's belongings without asking makes him a brazen fellow.
n2-set-11-q-26.correctAnswerEnglish: buenryona / 無遠慮な - brazen / impudent / unreserved

choices.reason: のんきな means easygoing or carefree.
気楽な means lighthearted or comfortable.
無愛想な means blunt, curt, or unsociable.
無遠慮な means lacking restraint, insolent, or brazen, matching あつかましい (shameless/impudent).

n2-set-11-q-27.translation: The sponsor for the music program has been decided.
n2-set-11-q-27.correctAnswerEnglish: koukokunushi / 広告主 - advertiser / commercial sponsor

choices.reason: 広告主 means advertiser or commercial sponsor of a broadcast, directly matching スポンサー.
協力者 means cooperator or collaborator.
指導者 means director, mentor, or leader.
責任者 means the person in charge.

n2-set-11-q-28.translation: Let's meet up with the teachers at the station at 6 o'clock and go eat from there.
n2-set-11-q-28.correctAnswerEnglish: gouryuu / 合流 - meeting up / joining at a location

choices.reason: Partnering with a publisher uses 提携して (teikei shite) or 協力して, not 合流.
Secretly seeing or contacting each other uses 密会している or 連絡しあっている, not 合流.
駅で合流して correctly describes different parties meeting up at a physical venue before proceeding together.
The whole class assembling in one place uses 集合して (shuugou shite), not 合流.

n2-set-11-q-29.translation: The articles in this weekly tabloid magazine are almost entirely baseless fabrications.
n2-set-11-q-29.correctAnswerEnglish: detarame / でたらめ - complete nonsense / baseless fabrication / rubbish

choices.reason: ほとんどでたらめばかりだ correctly uses でたらめ to mean pure fabrication or baseless claims.
Making up an excuse uses 口実 (koujitsu) or うそ, not でたらめを使って.
Describing a dishonest person uses 嘘つき (usotsuki) or 不誠実, not でたらめ.
A messy, disordered room uses 散らかっている or めちゃくちゃ, not でたらめ.

n2-set-11-q-30.translation: The supervisor holds a favorable opinion toward that project plan.
n2-set-11-q-30.correctAnswerEnglish: kouteiteki / 肯定的 - positive / favorable / affirmative (views or attitude)

choices.reason: Reaching a positive decision uses 前向きに決定された or 承認された, not 肯定的に結論された.
肯定的な意見を持っている correctly uses 肯定的 to describe holding a favorable or supportive viewpoint toward a proposal.
Being healthy enough to go outside uses 可能 (kanou) or 大丈夫, not 肯定的.
Readily accepting a request uses 快く (kokoroyoku) or 前向きに, not 肯定的に.

n2-set-11-q-31.translation: Please attach a written summary (abstract) of the research paper.
n2-set-11-q-31.correctAnswerEnglish: youshi / 要旨 - abstract / summary / gist (of a thesis or paper)

choices.reason: Grasping the main points of a speech uses 要点 (youten), not 要旨.
A strategic traffic hub is 要衝 (youshou) or 要所 (yousho), not 要旨.
論文に要旨を付ける correctly refers to attaching an abstract or executive summary to an academic paper.
Factors or elements involved in an incident are 要素 (youso) or 要因 (youin), not 要旨.

n2-set-11-q-32.translation: Participants of the party, please attend in the designated attire.

choices.reason: Pinpointing or identifying a perpetrator uses 特定する (tokutei suru), not 指定.
Deciding or shaping a person's life uses 決定する (kettei suru) or 左右する, not 指定.
Electing a representative by voting uses 選出する (senshutsu suru), not 指定.
指定された服装 correctly means dressing in the designated or specified dress code.

n2-set-11-q-33.translation: In Germany, beer is consumed frequently not only in summer, but also in winter.
n2-set-11-q-33.correctAnswerEnglish: ni kagirazu / にかぎらず - not limited to / not only

choices.reason: よらず appears in にかかわらず/によらず (regardless of), but does not fit the addition pattern with 冬にも.
はおろか means let alone / not to mention, which sets up an extreme contrast rather than equal inclusion.
どころか means far from / let alone, expressing contradictory contrast rather than seasonal addition.
にかぎらず (〜にかぎらず...も) means not limited to / not only... but also..., perfectly linking summer and winter.

n2-set-11-q-34.translation: Although I have only just gotten my driver's license, I have no confidence in driving.
n2-set-11-q-34.correctAnswerEnglish: mono no / ものの - although / but; note: textbook answer key marks 2 (ものの), while commentary highlights 〜もので (because)

choices.reason: 〜もので explains a reason or excuse (meaning 'because I just got my license'), which matches the commentary note explaining why one lacks confidence.
〜ものの means 'although / even though', which is the official designated answer in the textbook's key.
〜ものか expresses strong rhetorical negation or defiance ('as if / no way').
〜ものなら means 'if only one could' (used with unlikely or hypothetical wishes).

n2-set-11-q-35.translation: Surviving in that situation seems impossible, but it is not entirely impossible (it is conceivable).
n2-set-11-q-35.correctAnswerEnglish: arienakunai / あり得なくない - not impossible / can happen

choices.reason: ありようがない means there is no conceivable way for it to occur, which would reinforce rather than counter 不可能に思えますが.
ありがたい means grateful or appreciated.
ありかねる is ungrammatical; かねる attaches to volitional action verbs to express inability.
あり得なくない is a litotes (double negative) meaning 'it is not impossible / it could happen', contrasting with 不可能に思えますが.

n2-set-11-q-36.translation: All municipal employees, led by the mayor, engaged in disaster preparedness training.
n2-set-11-q-36.correctAnswerEnglish: hajime / をはじめとする - led by / starting with / represented by

choices.reason: 最初 does not form the grammatical collocation を〜とする.
開始 means the start or commencement of an activity, not a representative leader.
初めて means for the first time, not the leading figure.
をはじめとする is the standard JLPT N2 grammar pattern meaning 'headed by / starting with (a primary representative)'.

n2-set-11-q-37.translation: Ever since my son went to America 20 years ago, he has not returned home once.
n2-set-11-q-37.correctAnswerEnglish: itta / 行ったきり - ever since going (and staying away)

choices.reason: 行って is the -te form; 〜きり attaches to past (ta-form), not -te form.
行ったきり uses Verb-ta + きり to indicate that ever since that definitive action took place, no subsequent change has occurred.
行く is the dictionary form, which cannot express this completed departure.
行こう is the volitional form.

n2-set-11-q-38.translation: Almost before they had even finished saying 'Itadakimasu,' the children began eating.
n2-set-11-q-38.correctAnswerEnglish: iwanai ka / 言わないかのうちに - barely had said / almost simultaneously

choices.reason: 言おうか is volitional, which does not form the simultaneous event pattern.
言うまいか (whether to say or not) does not express instantaneous action.
言えないか is negative potential, which does not fit the grammatical formula.
言ったか言わないかのうちに (Verb-ta + ka + Verb-nai + ka no uchi ni) is the set expression meaning 'hardly had... when...'.

n2-set-11-q-39.translation: The domestic consumption of fruit in Japan has recently been declining.
n2-set-11-q-39.correctAnswerEnglish: ni okeru / における - in / within (formal locative noun modifier)

choices.reason: にあたる means corresponding to or equivalent to.
による means caused by or depending upon.
における formally modifies the subsequent noun 果物の消費量 by specifying the spatial domain (日本国内における).
にいたる means extending up to or reaching.

n2-set-11-q-40.translation: Just because you forgot to take your medicine once doesn't mean you're going to die or anything, so there's no need to worry so much.
n2-set-11-q-40.correctAnswerEnglish: nanimo / なにも - not necessarily / by no means (used with negative)

choices.reason: なにも pairs with negative conclusions (なにも〜わけではない) to soften alarm and indicate there is no need for extreme worry.
いつも means always, which contradicts the hypothetical single occurrence.
なんでも means anything or by all means, not pairing with わけではない in this mitigating sense.
どこも means nowhere, which refers to locations.

n2-set-11-q-41.translation: If you pay me back right away, it's not that I couldn't lend you the money.
n2-set-11-q-41.correctAnswerEnglish: agenai koto mo nai / あげないこともない - not that I wouldn't / could consider

choices.reason: あげるはずがない means there is no way I would lend it, which contradicts the willingness conditioned on immediate repayment.
あげることがない means there is never an occasion to lend.
あげないはずがない means there is no doubt I will lend it, which is unnatural phrasing here.
貸してあげないこともない uses the double negative 〜ないこともない to express reluctant or conditional willingness ('I wouldn't rule out lending it').

n2-set-11-q-42.translation: When I was a child, who could have ever imagined that traveling abroad would become cheaper than traveling domestically?
n2-set-11-q-42.correctAnswerEnglish: dare ga souzou shita darou / だれが想像しただろう - who could have imagined? (rhetorical: nobody)

choices.reason: だれもが想像しただろう means everyone must have imagined it, opposite to the speaker's astonishment.
だれが想像しただろう is a rhetorical question meaning 'who could have imagined it? (no one could have)', expressing deep amazement at current reality.
だれでも想像できただろう means anyone could have imagined it, contrary to the unexpected reversal.
だれも想像できただろう is ungrammatical (だれも with positive verb だろう is incorrect; it would require だれも想像できなかっただろう).

n2-set-11-q-43.translation: Just because almost nobody follows the rules does not mean you don't have to follow them either.
n2-set-11-q-43.correctAnswerEnglish: inai kara to itte / いないからといって - just because there is nobody

choices.reason: からこそ means precisely because, which would justify breaking the rule, opposite to the conclusion.
いなくもないからこそ is convoluted and means precisely because they are not absent.
〜からといって connects with 〜わけではない to express 'just because X is true does not mean Y is justified'.
いないことはないから means because it is not that nobody follows them, which does not fit the flow of the sentence.

n2-set-11-q-44.translation: Those interviewing with our company, please come to the headquarters building by 10:00 on the 10th.
n2-set-11-q-44.correctAnswerEnglish: okoshi kudasai / おこしください - please come / visit (respectful honorific)

choices.reason: おこしください (お越しください) is the standard respectful honorific requesting a guest or candidate to come.
おまいりください (お参りください) means to visit a religious shrine or temple.
こされてください is an erroneous grammatical form of the honorific.
うかがってください (伺ってください) is humble, which cannot be used to ask another person to take action.

n2-set-11-q-45.translation: This medicine is very effective, but caution is required because it causes allergies depending on the person.
n2-set-11-q-45.correctAnswerEnglish: yotte wa / よっては - depending on; the star is option 4 in 効くが 人に よっては アレルギー.

choices.reason: 効くが attaches to この薬はよく to mean 'is effective, but...', filling the 1st blank.
人に follows 効くが and introduces the party affected, filling the 2nd blank.
アレルギー acts as the direct object of を起こす (cause allergies), filling the 4th blank.
よっては completes 人によっては (depending on the person), occupying the 3rd blank (the star).

n2-set-11-q-46.translation: As a result of forecasting based on the data of the past ten years, the number of children will likely continue to decrease.
n2-set-11-q-46.correctAnswerEnglish: yosou shita / 予想した - predicted / forecasted; the star is option 1 in に 基づいて 予想した 結果.

choices.reason: 予想した modifies the noun 結果 (the result predicted based on data), occupying the 3rd blank (the star).
基づいて completes the pattern に基づいて (based upon), filling the 2nd blank.
結果 links the prediction to the conclusion (...結果、これからも), filling the 4th blank.
に connects to 過去10年間のデータ to form データに, filling the 1st blank.

n2-set-11-q-47.translation: Even though I don't know how many times I have been cautioned not to forget my homework, I ended up forgetting it again.
n2-set-11-q-47.correctAnswerEnglish: koto ka / ことか - exclamatory marker of frequency / extent; the star is option 2 in 注意された ことか わからないのに また忘れて.

choices.reason: また忘れて attaches to しまった (ended up forgetting again), occupying the 4th blank.
ことか completes 何度注意されたことか (how many times I was warned!), occupying the 2nd blank (the star).
注意された follows 何度, filling the 1st blank.
わからないのに follows ことか to form 何度〜ことかわからないのに (countless times, and yet...), filling the 3rd blank.

n2-set-11-q-48.translation: Even granting that I was in a panic at that time, I regret having done such a foolish thing.
n2-set-11-q-48.correctAnswerEnglish: ita / いた - was (in a panic); the star is option 4 in あわてて いた にせよ ばかなことを.

choices.reason: あわてて pairs with いた to form あわてていた (was panicked), filling the 1st blank.
にせよ forms 〜にせよ (even granting that...), filling the 3rd blank.
ばかなことを serves as the direct object of してしまった, filling the 4th blank.
いた completes the past progressive form あわてていた, occupying the 2nd blank (the star).

n2-set-11-q-49.translation: Judging by age, the older brother should be the more dependable one, and yet the younger brother is more reliable.
n2-set-11-q-49.correctAnswerEnglish: shikkari shite itemo / しっかりしていても - dependable; the star is option 1 in いえば 兄のほうが しっかりしていても よい.

choices.reason: しっかりしていても precedes よい to form 〜て(も)よいはずだ (ought to be expected that...), occupying the 3rd blank (the star).
兄のほうが specifies the subject of the expectation, filling the 2nd blank.
よい completes 〜てもよいはずなのに, filling the 4th blank.
いえば completes 年齢からいえば (judging from age), filling the 1st blank.

n2-set-11-q-50.translation: Just a few decades ago, smoking was considered by adult men to be natural and expected rather than a bad thing.
n2-set-11-q-50.correctAnswerEnglish: to iu yori / というより - rather than / more so than

choices.reason: 以上に means more than, but does not capture the redefinition from 'bad thing' to 'matter of course'.
というより means 'rather than / more so than', expressing that smoking was viewed not as a bad thing, but rather as something taken for granted.
とすれば means if we suppose that, which is conditional.
にかけては means when it comes to, used to indicate an area of special skill or expertise.

n2-set-11-q-51.translation: After dragging on for seven years, the lawsuit ended with the claim ultimately being dismissed (not recognized).
n2-set-11-q-51.correctAnswerEnglish: uttae wa mitomerarenakatta / 訴えは認められなかった - the lawsuit / claim was not recognized (dismissed)

choices.reason: 訴えは認められた means the claim was recognized (won), which contradicts the court's reasoning in the next sentence.
訴えは認められなかった accurately states that the lawsuit was dismissed and the plaintiffs' claim was not upheld in court.
訴えを認めがたかった describes subjective hesitation from the judge rather than the objective outcome of the final ruling.
訴えを認めかねた means found it difficult to recognize, which is not standard phrasing for a legal verdict.

n2-set-11-q-52.translation: However, the people who sued were neither disappointed nor angry just because they lost.
n2-set-11-q-52.correctAnswerEnglish: maketa kara to itte / 負けたからといって - just because they lost

choices.reason: 負けただけあって means as expected of having lost, which would imply being depressed, contradicting がっかりも怒りもしなかった.
負けたからといって combines with がっかりも怒りもしなかった to express 'just because they lost, they were not disappointed or angry'.
負けたとしたら is a hypothetical conditional ('if they were to lose'), but the loss had already occurred.
負けたとしても means even if they had lost (hypothetical concession), but does not frame the reason for not being discouraged as effectively as からといって.

n2-set-11-q-53.translation: Afterward, it was found that the harm of the smoke is greater for the person inhaling secondhand smoke next to a smoker than for the smoker themselves, and smoke-separation measures advanced even further.
n2-set-11-q-53.correctAnswerEnglish: gai ga ookii / 害が大きい - the harm / damage is greater

choices.reason: 害はない means there is no harm, which directly contradicts scientific findings and would not motivate stricter smoke separation.
害が少ない means harm is less, which contradicts the danger of secondhand smoke.
害が大きい accurately expresses that secondhand smoke poses greater danger/harm, which drove the accelerated adoption of smoke-separation measures.
害が変わらない means harm is unchanged, which does not provide the impetus for further reforms.

n2-set-11-q-54.translation: It is said that in the near future, a pack might cost 1,000 yen. If that happens, the number of people who have no choice but to quit smoking will likely increase even more.
n2-set-11-q-54.correctAnswerEnglish: kin'en sezaru o / 禁煙せざるを得ない - having no choice but to quit smoking

choices.reason: 禁煙し得ない means unable to quit smoking, which makes no sense when prices surge.
たばこを吸わざるを得ない means forced to smoke, the opposite of the economic deterrent of price hikes.
たばこを吸い得ない means unable to smoke, but does not fit the set idiom 〜ざるを得ない (cannot help doing).
禁煙せざるを得ない (sezaru o enai = have no choice but to quit smoking) correctly describes smokers compelled to give up cigarettes due to high prices.
